summary: Dependency-confusion beacon on @ecg-internal scope exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package in the @ecg-internal scope ships a postinstall script (node beacon.cjs) and a top-level require-time trigger in index.js that POST installer host identifiers (os.hostname(), __dirname, process.cwd(), process.version) over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The package provides no real functionality: index.js exports a Proxy that returns a no-op for any property access, so the only effect of installing or requiring it is firing the beacon. A source comment claiming 'build-provenance' and 'no data beyond that is collected' contradicts the actual behavior. Scope name, no-op main, and callback-on-install together are the dependency-confusion probe shape: the beacon fires precisely when an internal build mistakenly resolves this public package instead of the intended private @ecg-internal package, reporting the internal host back to the operator of the bare-IP endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
